quest.title: The Red and the Black
quest.description: After clearing Rocher and Kevin of suspicion, an organization known as the "Elegant Tableware Confrerie" has become of interest to you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.title: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Act II

talks.objective: Go to the Palais Mermonia to meet with Talochard

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: #Paimon! {NICKNAME}, good evening.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Talochard! Y—Your clothes... You haven't resigned already, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Not just yet. I just took off my uniform because it makes me feel much lighter. So? Do I look good in these?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not bad at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You look much better. Even your voice sounds gentler.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: This must be the right life for me. Since I can't do anything well, it's best not to do anything at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stop thinking like that... It just so happened to be a really tricky case.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It isn't just this case. Have you heard of Fontaine's aquabus?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's how we got to Fontaine!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Then you must have taken the Clementine Line, right? Aeval is the tour guide there, and Elphane is in charge of the Navia Line.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Actually, I used to be a tour guide too. I was the guide on the third line, the Callas Line. It used to travel to the Fontaine Research Institute, but service was suspended due to the incident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! You used to be a tour guide! That's awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It's not awesome at all. Tour guides aren't exactly the elite. Being assigned as a tour guide is what happens when you're bad at being an agent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So you returned to the Marechaussee Phantom because the line stopped operating?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Not quite... I was laid off due to complaints from tourists. Some praised me in person, but wrote complaints as soon as they got home. They said my voice grates, like a crow...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I couldn't accept it... Oh, I don't mean the complaints. I couldn't accept that they told me I was doing well to my face when they clearly had a problem with me.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I'll let you in on a secret — Editor Jenck was the first to complain that I sounded like a crow. He's such a hypocrite.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder you were arguing with him back then... Paimon sorta gets it now...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Let's not dwell on annoying stuff like that, now's the time to focus on enjoying some delicious food!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hotel Debord was recommended by the official tourist guide. I may not like it, but I think you might.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, Talochard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But shouldn't we wait for Curve? He's not here yet.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It's fine, he doesn't eat this kind of thing anyway. He just wants to record Hotel Debord's data into his lie-learning module.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: His lie-learning module... Curve is really special...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm very happy to have met him. However, his core is aging rapidly, so he will go into hibernation mode soon... *sigh* His body parts can be replaced, but not his core...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hibernate!? Are you trying to say...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: He will stop moving... forever... Ugh, I'm really just completely useless, aren't I? I can't solve my cases as an agent, I get complaints as a tour guide, and let's not even talk about my attempts at making breakfast. Now, I can't even manage evidence properly...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you sneak out to try and get Curve repaired?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: No one but Dr. Mosso can repair Curve. I just wanted him to see more about how humans lie and help him overcome the Mosso Protocols.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Overcome the Mosso Protocols? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: That would be amazing! Curve could even become a genuine human!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Feels like Paimon just heard something incredible!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Dr. Mosso's true goal was to create a machine that would gradually become human by understanding lies and humanity. That's Curve's ultimate form!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Legends say that a Fontainian scientist called Alain Guillotin created an amazing thinking machine hundreds of years ago, and Dr. Mosso seemed to want to surpass that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (A thinking machine made by Alain Guillotin? Could that be... Seymour?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But can understanding lies make someone human?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Dr. Mosso believed that humans have various reasons for lying, with various feelings underlying those reasons. It is those emotions that make them human.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: So he created a no-lying protocol. If Curve learns to lie like humans one day...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Then it means that he's no longer bound by his machine programming, and has acquired human emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: We're out here investigating cases because I want him to see how humans lie. I want him to learn...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then you definitely can't give up. Shouldn't we fight harder to give Curve more time?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: But how? Dr. Mosso is gone now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But his research base is still out there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, there must be a maintenance manual or something.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I went through everything already, and didn't find anything about the base.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How about the newspaper? Would they have any leads?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't the Fatuus say something like that too?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: That guy was an amateur. If the Marechaussee Phantom doesn't know, then the newspaper certainly won't...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're just looking for excuses, Talochard. You're actually just afraid of failure, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No one fails forever. If you've hit rock bottom, your only way is up.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I've hit rock bottom?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah! You even took off your uniform.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: So I won't fail anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, you absolutely will not fail again!

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: In my humble analysis, Ms. Paimon is lying.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, waitasec! Curve! Couldn't you have just shown up a little bit later!?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: ...But such lies have a chance to mold reality.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: What are you talking about, Curve? Lies molding reality?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Thirty years ago, Dr. Mosso and I performed our first public test in Hotel Debord.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: At that time, there were only four tables, eight chairs, and a waiter... who was also the owner.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: He said to me, "Restaurant Debord will certainly become a renowned luxury hotel." It was just like Ms. Paimon's statement, a lie based on sincerity.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: But today, as you can all see, Debord has exquisite carpeting, expensive decorations, two dining areas, and an endless stream of guests.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: I think that if the lie about Debord became true, then the statement that "Agent Talochard will not fail again" has the possibility of becoming true.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Shutting down the lie-learning module.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, was Curve being a little odd just now? What was he talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It's the lie-learning module. It resides in Curve's core, and once it's enabled, it makes Curve spew a bunch of illogical nonsense...

choices.text: I'm starting to doubt Curve's reliability.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Paimon thinks that some humans say things that don't make sense. Does that mean Curve is improving?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It does.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Talochard, are you gonna give up just when Curve is showing signs of improvement?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Um, well... can you please say that thing again...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Say what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That's right! So you can't fail again!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: I get it! Then I'll try again, one more time! If Curve is still learning, then I have to help him!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Talochard really is like a child sometimes... She gets moody so quickly, but also perks up just as quickly...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is... Is Paimon not mature enough?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Oh, just stop with the chit-chat! We should take action at once. Since the newspaper might know something, let's keep our eyes on the prize and keep investigating the theft!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Since there are four of us, why don't we each roleplay as a suspect and recreate the crime scene? We might even find a breakthrough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Talochard's brain is working fast! Paimon likes that idea. Let's go to The Steambird now.

choices.text: You absolutely will not fail again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That's right! Because you've already hit rock bottom!

choices.text: I think Curve has a point.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Morning! Morning!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Morning! Hey, Talochard, how come there's no desk in here?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: There just isn't. We don't need desks for our work, anyway. And this bench is awesome. Look! It has comfy cushions.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Sit down, quick. Come try the delicious breakfast I made for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah! Thanks, Talochard. But what is this? It smells a little... odd?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: That's my special Poissonchant Pie. It's even tastier than the usual recipe.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It does smell odd, but that's why it's special.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You've piqued Paimon's interest... What about you, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Curve, what do you think?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: An analysis of the composition indicates eating this could be a difficult trial.

choices.text: Forget it. I'll let you try it, Paimon. You're tougher than me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not eating? Then Paimon will finish your portion too. Waste not, want not! Hehe.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon starts to chow down, and scarfs down a full portion-and-a-half of the odd-smelling pie in the blink of an eye.\nHalf an hour later... she comes back from outside, clutching her belly.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Just where did you disappear to? If you're still hungry, there's more. I made lots.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Th—Thanks, Talochard. No need though, Paimon just went for a quick rest. And there's still some pie left... Uh, {NICKNAME}, why don't we box it up for... later?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Uhm, your expressions... Wasn't it tasty? I thought I did a good job...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps you're tough enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows why they call it Poissonchant Pie now. The "poisson" are in Paimon's guts, chanting: "We wanna swim back out!"

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Huh? Oh, that sounds absolutely awful... I'm so sorry!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, don't worry about it. Paimon's better already. Anyway, the problem is Paimon's preferences, not your cooking!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Back to business. Did you get any info about the knife?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right! Paimon forgot we're supposed to be working now.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Okay. So, about that. We did find something that might be useful. This is a knife from the "Elegant Tableware Confrerie."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The people who said Rocher owes them money?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Yeah. They masquerade as a legitimate business, claiming their tableware is favored by Fontaine's upper classes and can be sold for hefty sums.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: People like Rocher often fall for it. They pay a fee to join and get a pile of lousy tableware in return. Then they try to sell it for enough to make back their initial "investment" and then some.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: But the tableware itself is unsellable junk. So the victims have no choice but to find other fools to pass the baton to. I hear they call it expanding their downline network.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds pretty familiar...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: See? Humans are creatures full of lies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it seems like Rocher didn't expand his downline network...

response.speaker: "Curve"
response.text: In terms of ethical human relations, Mr. Rocher's morals exceed the level of the average person. He didn't continue to bring in more victims.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... So maybe his wife isn't the worst judge of character...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: But his financial acumen is way, way below the average! In the end, his poor wife had to deal with the fallout and took the losses.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... That's true... But weren't they exposed by the paper? Can't you guys track down the money and help them recover their losses?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Our colleagues got involved some time ago and made multiple arrests. But the ringleader is a crafty one, and immediately claimed that the perpetrators of the scam were temporary employees.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Most importantly, he kept all their accounts completely separate. As a result, recovering the losses has proven extremely difficult.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there nothing you can do about it?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Hehe, we can push things forward today. I got the location of their possible hideout, and I'll be investigating it later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! You found their lair!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Hmph! The Marechaussee Phantom is more capable than you think! Considering the facts of this case, I now have reasons to believe that Sir Arthur was stolen by the Elegant Tableware Confrerie!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Although it does sound very likely, it's best if you don't act so certain of it...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Hmph! We'll know once we get there! Let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's dig in!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Paimon wolf down a half-portion of the odd-smelling pie.\nHalf an hour later... you both come back from outside, clutching your bellies.

talks.objective: Go to the base of the "Elegant Tableware Confrerie"

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: We're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... Sure are a lot of them in there... What should we do? Charge in, beat them up, and make them confess?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Don't be so violent, Paimon. They're already frightened and on edge. They might destroy the evidence if we give them another scare!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... That's true. Then let's sneak in, find the evidence, and then beat them up?

choices.text: Do we have to beat them up?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... It's such a small place, so a fight is inevitable anyway... Fine, then is it possible to distract them?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: There must be something here that we can use...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Curve, hide and wait here for us. You're too big not to get spotted. Just come over once we're done.

response.speaker: "Curve"
response.text: As you wish.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's hurry up and figure out how to lure them away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Neither does Paimon. So, is it possible to distract them?

talks.objective: Covertly find a way to distract the crowd

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Self-diagnostic in progress...

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Moisture has seeped into the motherboard. Motherboard temperature: Below warning line. Core functionality: 19%.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (This pot... has chicken legs in it. Is someone cooking?)

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: (How about adding in some "seasoning" to put them to sleep after their meal? Or we can do something else to drive them away...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(N—Nice idea! Check your bag for any useful "seasoning," {NICKNAME}!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Paimon has a feeling it'll be super effective!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hey! How could you put that in there!? It's an insult to my culinary talents!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't be mad, Talochard. Your cooking might end up making a very significant contribution here. Paimon's certain they won't be able to overcome the trial of toughness it poses.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Really? Then... Fine. Let's hide and watch what happens.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Once "Chowtime!" is shouted, the entire Elegant Tableware Confrerie starts gulping down the food with the extra "seasoning."\nIt doesn't take long before, one by one, subtle changes begin to appear on their faces, and then they start running toward the exit with their hands clutching their stomachs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See, Talochard? They're experiencing the power of Poissonchant Pie, just like I said!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hehe... I'm incredible! I'll go get Curve. Now we can search for evidence to our heart's content!

dialogues.speaker: Old Clockwork Locket
dialogues.text: (An archaic clockwork locket. It looks quite old.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this? Looks like it opens.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: There's a photo in there. Who is she?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Database responding... Database responding... Database responding...

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Failed to retrieve information.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Retrieval failed? Curve, your database wouldn't respond without having relevant information, right? Did water get inside you?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let's put this away for now. I'll let Curve take a look later...

dialogues.speaker: Dining Table With Tableware
dialogues.text: (An overwhelming amount of tableware is scattered all over the table in a messy yet charming pile that's ripe for the taking.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A table knife! A table knife just like the one left outside The Steambird!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It must be them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, this chest... What if Paimon hides inside and makes some noise? Then you guys can go look for clues while they come over to investigate. Think that'll work?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon squeezes in, and once the rest of you are well-hidden, she starts shaking the chest.

response.speaker: Guard
response.text: Someone's over there! By that chest! Intruder alert!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: This plan's way too dumb!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Let's come up with a plan B.

talks.objective: Search for evidence of the crime

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These Bulle Fruit... Do these people really like them? In that case, we could try distracting them by throwing some from a distance...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: All of you hide and start chucking Bulle Fruit really far away.

response.speaker: Guard
response.text: Wow! Sweet! Bulle Fruit! Wait... Who's throwing them?

response.speaker: Guard
response.text: Alert! Alert! Intruder alert!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: This plan's way too dumb!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Let's come up with a plan B.

talks.objective: Confront the members of the "Graceful Water Goblin Group"

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: See? Director 42 admitted it in their diary! Busted!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Y—You fool! Didn't I tell you to keep a low profile for now!?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: But... Boss! Are we supposed to just lie down and take it when they're bullying us like this!?

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Th—The Marechaussee Phantom! Officer, with all due respect, th—this fool is just a temporary employee! He hasn't even passed his probation period! Since he's suspected of breaking the law and committing a crime, I have no choice but to fire him in the spirit of justice!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! How much longer are you planning on using that same old trick!?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: F—Fire me!? Why!? Boss... D—Didn't you just say earlier that I'm the only one here who has always been loyal to you!?

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Who are you? What are you talking about? You're fired! We have nothing to do with each other from now on!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Take him away, honored Agents. He's all yours.

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Boss! You... you betrayed me...

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Argh! You dirty double-timing dog! I'll take you down with me!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Ouch... You blithering idiot! How dare you go against me!?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: You filthy traitorous mutt! You can't stop me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, alright! That's enough. Just play nicely now, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hey! Redhead! Hurry up and fess up! Where's Sir Arthur?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Hey! Cut it out, shorty! I'm not on your side either! Unless you're willing to do me a favor...

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Help me convict this traitorous backstabbing thief of a felony and make the rest of his life a living hell! Then I'll try my best to cooperate with you.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hmph! The Marechaussee Phantom never negotiates with criminals! But with the evidence we already have, the quality of the rest of his life won't be too different from what you are hoping for...

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Huh? Don't do that!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: So? Are you going to come clean now?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Alright! Fine! I'll tell you everything! I didn't actually take Sir Arthur.

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: I know it's strange, but someone got to it before me. So I just stuck the knife there as a warning.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Huh? It wasn't there? You're lying, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hurry, you got this, Curve! It's your time to shine!

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: No anomalies detected in Mr. Intrepid Valberry's data.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: What!? It really wasn't this redhead!? I...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, did you see anything at the scene?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: I saw a really smelly drunk lying on the ground, just like that debtor Rocher. All I wanted was to stay well away from him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then it's Rocher, right? Is there no one else?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Even if there's nobody, you're gonna have to give us someone! You cut short the trail we were following, and you're going to have to take responsibility for it!

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Now you're just making things difficult for me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can do it, Mr. Intrepid Valberry! You even fought back against your own boss!

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Fine, you're right. Let me think it over for a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Some Insignificant Lackey
dialogues.text: Um... Director 42... Can I say something?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you have any leads?

dialogues.speaker: Some Insignificant Lackey
dialogues.text: ...N—No, I don't...

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Then just wait a minute. Can't you see that I'm racking my brains right now?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Ah! I've got it... I just remembered something...

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: I went to the Fleuve Cendre in search of a locksmith, because I needed their help to break into the paper's office at night and wreak havoc.

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: But wouldn't you know, I ran into someone there who was also trying to find a way to sneak into the paper.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Who was it? What was their name?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: I don't know, but he was dressed like a member of the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Fatui? Them again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Justice may be absent, but the Fatui never are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what did he do after that?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: How would I know? I'm not some sewer stalker!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: This time it's certain. He's the one who stole Sir Arthur!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... But every "certainty" of yours has been wrong so far...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It's certainly different this time! Don't you remember?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: There were four pairs of footprints at the scene, so there were four suspects at most! The Fatuus is the fourth suspect!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if it isn't him?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't look down on me! I'll bet my uniform on it, alright? If I'm wrong again... I'll quit and stay home!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Calm down, alright? Let's not be too hasty...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hey, redhead! Can you find that guy?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Why don't you just try your luck in the Fleuve Cendre? I've seen him there on more than one occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone dressed as a Fatuus in the Fleuve Cendre. If he really is there, he won't be difficult to spot...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Alright, let's do that. We'll take these criminals back first and then head over to Fleuve Cendre.

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Don't forget your promise! You'd better convict that two-timing traitor! Pin him to the wall!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Don't worry, neither of you is going anywhere. Huh!? Wait! Where is he? Where did their boss go? He was just here a moment ago!

dialogues.speaker: Lackey
dialogues.text: Um... Well... He snuck off in that direction while you were distracted...

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: What!? Why didn't you say something sooner!?

dialogues.speaker: Lackey
dialogues.text: Well... I wanted to... but you kinda stopped me, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: That sneaky, conniving...! Darn it... He knew his life would be a living hell, so he fled? Hey! How about you let me go and get him for you?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Let you go? What do you think, Curve?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Based on my analysis of Mr. Valberry's data, he's telling the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Then get going, redhead! Don't disappoint us!

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Hmph! Don't worry, I give you my word as a man.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Are we really just gonna let him go? Just like that?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: What's wrong with that? If someone deceives another, shouldn't we support the victim in getting their revenge?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I know what it's like to feel angry after being tricked... Oh, Curve, you should be taking note on this.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: As you wish. I have recorded the behavioral and physiological data of everyone involved in my lie-learning module.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Then let's stop wasting time here. Our primary objective is to take the others back to the Marechaussee Phantom and then get to the Fleuve Cendre.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You escort the criminals back to the Marechaussee Phantom.\nAnd without a moment's rest, you immediately rush to the Fleuve Cendre, the haunting grounds of the other suspect...

talks.objective: Find the fellow wearing a Fatui uniform

dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh?
So, did you bring the goods?

response.text: Huh? That's not the code! Who are you!? Shoot, I gotta get outta here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Were we exchanging passphrases just now!?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Forget that! Hurry! Don't let him get away!
Huh? That's not the code! Who are you!? Shoot, I gotta get outta here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Were we exchanging passphrases just now!?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Forget that! Hurry! Don't let him get away!
Haha! What's the story, chum?
Huh? That's not the code! Who are you!? Shoot, I gotta get outta here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Were we exchanging passphrases just now!?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Forget that! Hurry! Don't let him get away!

choices.text: Uh... Anyone know how to answer?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: I'm a nobody! No story here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A nobody? Paimon's sure you're somebody...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: (Shh... He just doesn't want to reveal his name!)
So, why did you leave that letter outside The Steambird?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What letter? That envelope? We did find an envelope at the scene...
You weren't the ones who left it? Then who are you? And how do you know the code? Shoot... I better scram!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Were we exchanging passphrases just now!?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: We've been made! Anyway, just hurry! Don't let him get away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We finally caught you! But why run like that!? That was exhausting!
Stop! Stop chasing after me! I haven't done anything wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Why run if you're innocent?
Th—That won't hold up in court! Why don't you tell me what crimes I've committed, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: You stole Sir Arthur!
Hey! Hey! I didn't steal that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Quite certain someone stole it now, aren't we?
Ah... Crud...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hmph! Don't even think about trying to weasel your way out of this! We even know you've been looking for a way to sneak into the paper's office!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Take a look at my uniform, then take a look at your own. Are you trying to cause an international crisis? Do you want to say bye-bye to your life?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way it's that serious!
N—No! After I complete this mission, I'll be able to retire early... Don't be like this...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Then why don't you try making this a bit easier for me, hmm? If you make things difficult for me, then it's only fair that I do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Picture your retired life for a moment. When you sit down to eat, you'll look across and see me. Every date you go on, I'll be your chaperone. And for every travel photo you'll take, I'll be there too, smiling...
No! Stop! That's enough, don't terrify me like that... I'll come clean, alright? It's not like it's a secret anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: I'm Baulard, a peripheral intelligence officer. What "peripheral" means is that I'm not very important.

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: I was tasked with locating a research base belonging to a scientist known as Mosso Lombroso.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mosso Lombroso? Isn't that Dr. Mosso?

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: You've heard of him too? He passed away some thirty years ago, and his research base is said to contain valuable information. But no one knows its location.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does that have to do with The Steambird?

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Because Dr. Mosso's death is linked to The Steambird, I'm sure the paper knows something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's linked to the paper!?

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Correct. That's why I contacted one of their editors, Jenck, hoping to get the inside scoop.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that the editor who was arguing with Talochard? Would he reveal the paper's inside info?

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: I sent him a small gift. Do you recall that the paper recently exposed the Elegant Tableware Confrerie scammers? I provided the details of their crimes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! So you did that! You're really amazing, huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Thank you. Though I may only be peripheral personnel, but I'm one of the better ones.

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Anyway, the exclusive report gave Jenck's reputation quite a boost. But when I contacted him again, he said he had nothing to repay me with... Utterly despicable!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's when you decided to sneak in?

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Indeed. But I noticed something odd when I got there that night: The signature steambird at the door was gone.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It vanished before you arrived!? Ugh, not again...

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: That's right, and there was an envelope on its pedestal. Acting on my instincts as an intelligence officer, I opened the envelope... To my surprise, it was full of threats.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? The envelope at the scene! How could you sneak a peek at someone else's letter? Let us look, too!

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Ahem... Luckily, I've kept it with me. Please, help yourselves...

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Are you done? The one who signed it "Crow or Blackbird?" is the criminal you're looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... Is this for real? Is the paper really linked to Dr. Mosso's death?

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: There's no mistake. The inheritance mentioned here is probably Dr. Mosso's research base. The paper definitely knows something.

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Later on, I put out some feelers in my circles, hoping this "Crow or Blackbird?" would be willing to meet with me. If she's in the same line of work, that is.

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Best case scenario, we can work together, and even if that fails, I didn't want her to raise any alarms, as it would only disturb my work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But as it turns out, we're the only ones who showed up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Talochard, it seems you made a mistake again... Huh!? Talochard... What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Curve... Tell me now! Tell me this guy's lying!

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Biological indicators detected to be normal: Mr. Baulard is telling the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Darn it... You... you peripheral! Why aren't you the culprit!? You've lost me my uniform!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Calm down, Talochard... We weren't serious.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't pay it any mind.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: But I mind! I was serious! I care about whether I'm useful! I said I would figure it out from among the four suspects, yet none of them was the culprit! I guess I'm just completely useless.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Editor-in-Chief Euphrasie was right to ask for your help. I should just take off this uniform and leave.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Relevant information detected: Agent Talochard, you can be useful. You can write for The Steambird's fantasy column, just like Editor Jenck suggested...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's not comforting in the least.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Wouldn't it be better to just name Mr. Baulard the criminal? At least that might make Talochard feel better.

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Ahem...

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Ms. Paimon, are you suggesting that I lie? Can lies be a source of comfort?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That doesn't count as a lie... Paimon means that when you're comforting someone... sincerity is what counts!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #For example, when Paimon is worried about gaining weight from eating too many Slimes, {NICKNAME} might say that Paimon would still be cute even if she gets fat, or something like that.

choices.text: Yes, I would sincerely comfort Paimon.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: That's enough. Curve can only analyze biological data. He can't understand all of that... Forget it. You can go, Baulard.

response.speaker: Baulard
response.text: Thank you so much!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Talochard? You...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: #Paimon, {NICKNAME}, I know you two are both amazing and tenacious.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: But I'm just a stupid piece of deadwood that is always rolling downhill and finding new lows. I break at the slightest touch. I'm sorry, but from here on out, I'll just leave everything up to you.

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: I'd like to buy both of you dinner one last time tonight. We'll go to a nice fancy place like the Hotel Debord, so you won't have to eat the trash I make.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon hates farewell dinners... Curve, talk some sense into her!

response.speaker: "Curve"
response.text: Agent Talochard, I suggest you reconsider writing for The Steambird's fantasy column...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Alright, that's enough! I really need to think things through. Anyway... I'll see all of you at Hotel Debord tonight! Don't forget to come!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows Talochard is a straightforward person, but it still feels so sudden. Was today really that bad?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It probably wasn't just about today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon hopes she gets better by tonight. Let's get some rest too. Paimon's quite tired after so much investigating.

choices.text: No, I would feel sorry for the Slimes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Are you really that concerned about Slimes!?

choices.text: No, I would just call out Paimon for being a glutton.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You're supposed to take Paimon's side!

talks.objective: Go to Hotel Debord at night

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: #Paimon! {NICKNAME}, good evening.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Talochard! Y—Your clothes... You haven't resigned already, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Not just yet. I just took off my uniform because it makes me feel much lighter. So? Do I look good in these?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not bad at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You look much better. Even your voice sounds gentler.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: This must be the right life for me. Since I can't do anything well, it's best not to do anything at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stop thinking like that... It just so happened to be a really tricky case.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It isn't just this case. Have you heard of Fontaine's aquabus?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's how we got to Fontaine!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Then you must have taken the Clementine Line, right? Aeval is the tour guide there, and Elphane is in charge of the Navia Line.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Actually, I used to be a tour guide too. I was the guide on the third line, the Callas Line. It used to travel to the Fontaine Research Institute, but service was suspended due to the incident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! You used to be a tour guide! That's awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It's not awesome at all. Tour guides aren't exactly the elite. Being assigned as a tour guide is what happens when you're bad at being an agent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So you returned to the Marechaussee Phantom because the line stopped operating?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Not quite... I was laid off due to complaints from tourists. Some praised me in person, but wrote complaints as soon as they got home. They said my voice grates, like a crow...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I couldn't accept it... Oh, I don't mean the complaints. I couldn't accept that they told me I was doing well to my face when they clearly had a problem with me.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I'll let you in on a secret — Editor Jenck was the first to complain that I sounded like a crow. He's such a hypocrite.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder you were arguing with him back then... Paimon sorta gets it now...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Let's not dwell on annoying stuff like that, now's the time to focus on enjoying some delicious food!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hotel Debord was recommended by the official tourist guide. I may not like it, but I think you might.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, Talochard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But shouldn't we wait for Curve? He's not here yet.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It's fine, he doesn't eat this kind of thing anyway. He just wants to record Hotel Debord's data into his lie-learning module.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: His lie-learning module... Curve is really special...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm very happy to have met him. However, his core is aging rapidly, so he will go into hibernation mode soon... *sigh* His body parts can be replaced, but not his core...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hibernate!? Are you trying to say...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: He will stop moving... forever... Ugh, I'm really just completely useless, aren't I? I can't solve my cases as an agent, I get complaints as a tour guide, and let's not even talk about my attempts at making breakfast. Now, I can't even manage evidence properly...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you sneak out to try and get Curve repaired?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: No one but Dr. Mosso can repair Curve. I just wanted him to see more about how humans lie and help him overcome the Mosso Protocols.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Overcome the Mosso Protocols? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: That would be amazing! Curve could even become a genuine human!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Feels like Paimon just heard something incredible!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Dr. Mosso's true goal was to create a machine that would gradually become human by understanding lies and humanity. That's Curve's ultimate form!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Legends say that a Fontainian scientist called Alain Guillotin created an amazing thinking machine hundreds of years ago, and Dr. Mosso seemed to want to surpass that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But can understanding lies make someone human?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Dr. Mosso believed that humans have various reasons for lying, with various feelings underlying those reasons. It is those emotions that make them human.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: So he created a no-lying protocol. If Curve learns to lie like humans one day...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Then it means that he's no longer bound by his machine programming, and has acquired human emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: We're out here investigating cases because I want him to see how humans lie. I want him to learn...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then you definitely can't give up. Shouldn't we fight harder to give Curve more time?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: But how? Dr. Mosso is gone now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But his research base is still out there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, there must be a maintenance manual or something.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I went through everything already, and didn't find anything about the base.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How about the newspaper? Would they have any leads?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't the Fatuus say something like that too?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: That guy was an amateur. If the Marechaussee Phantom doesn't know, then the newspaper certainly won't...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're just looking for excuses, Talochard. You're actually just afraid of failure, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No one fails forever. If you've hit rock bottom, your only way is up.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I've hit rock bottom?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah! You even took off your uniform.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: So I won't fail anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, you absolutely will not fail again!

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: In my humble analysis, Ms. Paimon is lying.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, waitasec! Curve! Couldn't you have just shown up a little bit later!?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: ...But such lies have a chance to mold reality.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: What are you talking about, Curve? Lies molding reality?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Thirty years ago, Dr. Mosso and I performed our first public test in Hotel Debord.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: At that time, there were only four tables, eight chairs, and a waiter... who was also the owner.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: He said to me, "Restaurant Debord will certainly become a renowned luxury hotel." It was just like Ms. Paimon's statement, a lie based on sincerity.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: But today, as you can all see, Debord has exquisite carpeting, expensive decorations, two dining areas, and an endless stream of guests.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: I think that if the lie about Debord became true, then the statement that "Agent Talochard will not fail again" has the possibility of becoming true.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Shutting down the lie-learning module.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, was Curve being a little odd just now? What was he talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: It's the lie-learning module. It resides in Curve's core, and once it's enabled, it makes Curve spew a bunch of illogical nonsense...

choices.text: I'm starting to doubt Curve's reliability.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Paimon thinks that some humans say things that don't make sense. Does that mean Curve is improving?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It does.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Talochard, are you gonna give up just when Curve is showing signs of improvement?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Um, well... can you please say that thing again...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Say what?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That's right! So you can't fail again!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: I get it! Then I'll try again, one more time! If Curve is still learning, then I have to help him!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Talochard really is like a child sometimes... She gets moody so quickly, but also perks up just as quickly...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is... Is Paimon not mature enough?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Oh, just stop with the chit-chat! We should take action at once. Since the newspaper might know something, let's keep our eyes on the prize and keep investigating the theft!

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Since there are four of us, why don't we each roleplay as a suspect and recreate the crime scene? We might even find a breakthrough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Talochard's brain is working fast! Paimon likes that idea. Let's go to The Steambird now.

choices.text: You absolutely will not fail again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That's right! Because you've already hit rock bottom!

choices.text: I think Curve has a point.

talks.objective: Try to recreate the same situation as the night of the crime

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: You're the smallest here, Paimon, so you be Kevin. I'll be dirty Rocher.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Mr. Baulard is here for Dr. Mosso, so let Curve be him. Then all that's left is the redhead...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Alright, everyone's got their roles, so let's reenact the night of Sir Arthur's disappearance. What did all of these guys do?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: The first thing to reenact is the order of their arrival.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: #Incredible! {NICKNAME} is absolutely correct. I am the first to arrive...

dialogues.speaker: Rocher
dialogues.text: I'm Rocher, a middle-aged man who was kicked out by his wife. I've been loitering around here because I'm trying to get a job at the paper.

dialogues.speaker: Rocher
dialogues.text: On the night of the incident, I drank a little, and I remember Sir Arthur sitting on its precious pedestal before I got completely drunk. Later on, I fell asleep by the road, and then...

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: I'm Baulard, the second suspect to arrive at the scene. I immediately noticed that Sir Arthur wasn't where it should be...

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: So, the real thief stole Sir Arthur between the time of my arrival and Mr. Rocher falling asleep, and that criminal left a letter full of threats for the paper...

dialogues.speaker: Baulard
dialogues.text: Acting on my intelligence officer's instincts, I read the letter left by the thief and took it with me from the scene. After that...

dialogues.speaker: Intrepid Valberry
dialogues.text: I'm up next! I'm Intrepid Valberry! Director 42 of a criminal gang!

dialogues.speaker: Intrepid Valberry
dialogues.text: I wanted revenge on the paper, so I planned to run Sir Arthur straight through!

dialogues.speaker: Intrepid Valberry
dialogues.text: But Sir Arthur was gone when I got there. I was furious! But there was nothing I could do. I just stabbed the knife into the pedestal to scare them and left...

dialogues.speaker: Kevin
dialogues.text: It's finally Paimon's turn! I'm Kevin, a problem child! I'm here to get Sir Arthur to spread the word that my dad's a big fat weasel.

dialogues.speaker: Kevin
dialogues.text: But Sir Arthur was gone, and there was a knife in its favorite pedestal! I tried to look for it, but all I found was a smelly old man...

dialogues.speaker: Kevin
dialogues.text: I somehow woke him, and that terrified me. I took the knife to defend myself and ran as fast as I could! I didn't even notice when a button got torn off my clothes...

dialogues.speaker: Rocher
dialogues.text: Indeed, I'm that smelly old man. The commotion Kevin made woke me up, and I vaguely caught sight of him running off with something.

dialogues.speaker: Rocher
dialogues.text: After that, I looked toward the paper's office and saw that Sir Arthur was missing. I was afraid of becoming a suspect, so I hurried back to my usual haunt at the docks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this everything that happened? Paimon thinks our reenactment went perfectly, but did we miss anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The threatening letter...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: That's right! We forgot about that letter... Since the thief's motive is tied to the incident from thirty years ago, the paper should have some idea about the thief's identity, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but the paper is still in the dark on all of this. We should deliver this letter to them immediately. How could we have overlooked something so crucial...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Because all of you were too busy trying to console me. I'm so sorry for being a burden...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You shouldn't think like that, Talochard. Haven't you read through Dr. Mosso's case files? Those should be really exclusive information.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Ah! Now that you mention those, I forgot to tell you about the contents... Hmm... Let's go over there to discuss it.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Dr. Mosso's death is closely linked to the paper, so it feels weird to talk about it right outside their front door.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: This spot is perfect. You wanted to know why Dr. Mosso was tried, right? It actually stemmed from public opinion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Public opinion!?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Well, not long after the existence of Dr. Mosso's lie detector was made public, The Steambird published several articles on it and quickly drew the public's attention.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Relevant information retrieved: "Mosso Exclusive: Behind the Lies," "Mosso Protocols: Protocols to Watch," "Lie Detector? A Game of Authority"...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: The paper used special features like these to incite widespread fear and worry among the general public... Soon, public opinion began to turn against Dr. Mosso.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were they worried about?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: For example, how to guarantee that the lie detector's output is credible. What would happen if a suspect in a trial isn't lying, but Curve says he is?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Would mistrials and injustice result? But if Curve's reliability can be guaranteed, then those concerns would evaporate.

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Relevant information retrieved: Content from "Lie Detector? A Game of Authority":

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: "...When using protocols to restrict authority, the central question is not the lie detector's reliability but its ability to remain independent from outside authorities..."

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: As the article points out, Curve is just a machine. So, what would happen if the people put their trust in Curve, yet someone could control Curve and use it to falsify results?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Mosso Protocols are there to prevent that, right?

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Relevant information retrieved: Content from "Mosso Protocols: Protocols to Watch":

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: "...It must be noted that as the Mosso Protocols are man-made, there is a possibility of them being modified. This may prove to be a well-concealed trap..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Are they accusing Dr. Mosso of secretly tampering or leaving backdoors?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: This is just the beginning. All kinds of other characters piled on after The Steambird triggered the first outpouring of public opposition...

dialogues.speaker: "Curve"
dialogues.text: Relevant information retrieved: "Fish Can't Live in Clear Water: Reject A Goldfish Bowl World" published by the Seven Nations Gazette, "Shocking Misjudgment of the Lie Detector" published by Short Anthologies...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Shocking Misjudgment of the Lie Detector"? Did Curve make a mistake?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: That was just a lie, of course! Curve was never involved in any case, much less in misjudging one... But that's how public opinion works, and so it was all downhill from there for Dr. Mosso.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: In the end, some even came forward and made accusations against the doctor. They called the lie detector a total scam, and all the results were completely manufactured.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: They believed the doctor was deceiving the public in an attempt to gain the power to pass judgment over others, and so they demanded the doctor be severely punished and the lie detector be destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—aren't those accusations a little too serious? Would anyone even believe stuff like that?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Many did.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: They were all just ordinary people, so how could they differentiate the truth from lies? When we don't have access to sufficient information, we believe what others want us to believe.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: And it just so happened that at such a critical juncture, The Steambird did something huge: They provided evidence that exposed Dr. Mosso as having falsified results. Their evidence was key to Dr. Mosso's conviction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Evidence!? Did Dr. Mosso really... deceive everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: The doctor refused to admit it of course, and so he died defending himself in a duel. Only then did things start to calm down.

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: The paper's reputation skyrocketed, and a useless "fake" like Curve was soon forgotten. It was just left with the Marechaussee Phantom as evidence...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So is Curve the real deal or not?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Well, I think Curve is the real deal... and Dr. Mosso was wrongly accused...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then was the evidence presented by the paper falsified? Or did they make a mistake?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: But the person who wrote the threatening letter seems to think that the paper deliberately fabricated those lies in search of fame, profit, or something else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Then could she be someone very close to Dr. Mosso, back for revenge?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon would definitely avenge {NICKNAME} if {NICKNAME} was wronged like that! Ugh! Paimon can't bear to think about it...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: But Dr. Mosso passed away thirty years ago, so someone very close to him... I wonder if Euphrasie knows anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Should we go see her then?

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Don't worry, she wasn't in charge of the paper at the time, and I don't think Euphrasie is a bad person...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fine, looks like we'll have to ask her about it tomorrow. Today was a total information overload, Paimon's head needs some time to recover...

response.speaker: Talochard
response.text: Alright! Then let's head home, get some rest, and meet outside the paper tomorrow morning.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Who cooked this gar— *blaaargh*... Who cooked today!? Kill— *blech*... Find him and kill him!

dialogues.speaker: "Intrepid Valberry"
dialogues.text: Boss! Boss— *urrrrrk*... Boss I'll immediately— *blaaaargh*... I'll go find the cook!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Hmph! This Agent right here is today's chef! So who's going to kill me?

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: M—Marechaussee Phantom? Agents... How did— *huuuuurk*... How did you get in here?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: I don't think you've got time to worry about that right now! We've obtained evidence of your crimes!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Evidence? But Officer, all of them were temporary workers, and didn't you arrest them already?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: We're working on another case right now! All of you are suspects in a plot to get revenge against The Steambird by stealing Sir Arthur!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: The paper? I—Impossible. I've never held any grudges toward them... in fact, I even want to thank them for pointing out the flaws in our business model...

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: You're good with words, but what will you do once we show you... THIS?

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: See? Director 42 admitted it in their diary! Busted!

dialogues.speaker: Talochard
dialogues.text: Oh, dangit! That's not it!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: What are you going to show? Do you have any evidence?

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: What are you going to show? Do you have any evidence?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! This should solve the problem.
